content.text:
Nature and science facts about leopards

The flower-shaped markings (rosettes) all over a leopard's body are perfect for hiding among the shadows of the leaves. It climbs trees so well that it cleverly hauls its catch up into the branches so lions and hyenas can't steal it. As a solitary hunter that lives alone, it's skilled at a stealthy hunt — creeping up silently and pouncing in an instant — and it has eyes that see well even in the dark, along with strong legs and sharp claws.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Why does a leopard haul its prey up a tree?
A. To keep lions and hyenas from stealing it, the leopard drags its catch up into the branches. It's very clever.

Q. What do a leopard's markings look like?
A. They're petal-like "rosette" markings. They're great for camouflage, hiding the body among the shadows of the leaves.

Q. How can we observe them at home?
A. Comparing the markings of leopards, cheetahs, and jaguars, and talking about "how clever it is to store prey up a tree," both work well.
